acceptanceCriteria: When the event deadline expires, the fallback text names which phase ran out of time and includes any measurements already taken (git status path count and duration if the probe completed; load average where the OS exposes it cheaply). It names 'host load' or 'large worktree' only when a measurement supports it, and otherwise says 'not measured'.
No extra probe pushes the hook past its deadline: a test proves that the measurement adds bounded time, and the spec text in agent-harness-integration-v0 is updated in the same change.
Tests cover the load-dominated case (fast status, deadline hit) and the dirty-set-dominated case.
body: Observed 2026-10-16 08:42 (orchestrator, Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 0, Claude Code Stop and UserPromptSubmit hooks in /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint): the hooks repeatedly fail open with corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-deadline. The notice says the usual causes are a large uncommitted set or heavy load and that it 'did not measure either', then tells the user to run git status. Measured at the same time: `git status --short` returned 4,820 paths in 0.37 s real, and the load average was 64.57/96.45/69.59 (5 builder lanes plus closeout gates). So the cause was host load, not the dirty set, but the user cannot tell that from the notice and may be steered toward committing or stashing load-bearing state. Expected: the fallback reports cheap measurements it already has or can take within its budget (elapsed time per phase, the 1-minute load average where available, the dirty path count when the status probe finished), and names the dominant cause. Actual: two unmeasured guesses. This is the same failure class as V1-1120/V1-1422/V1-1280 (all completed); fail-open is correct, so this is a diagnosis gap, not a correctness bug.
title: Hooks: dogfood-event-deadline fallback should report the measured cause (host load, dirty path count) instead of naming two guesses
